sm: The show opens with a string of outages that has prompted a strong response from national security officials trying to calm public fears, including a claim of 98 percent confidence that adversaries are not behind them. Hosts Georgia Howe and John Bickley introduce the Thursday, November 19th edition. The other headlines are Anthropic going public today at an eye-popping initial price, and what to expect from the Democrats set to take over the governorship of Texas.

White House correspondent Mary Margaret Olohan reports on Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin's congressional hearing on the outages. Mullin said DHS is 98 percent confident they were not caused by a cyber attack, and intelligence and FBI officials said they found no evidence of coordinated malicious activity. One congressional official suggested some outages came from companies patching vulnerabilities found by artificial intelligence, though Olohan says many people want more answers. She also discusses Vice President Vance pulling out of a New York Times event, with his office saying he was needed in Washington, while the Times reported the president is unhappy with Vance's comments on the midterm losses. Finally, she previews Trump's meetings in China, including a three-way session with Xi and Putin and a one-on-one with Putin, covering trade, Ukraine, sanctions and nuclear weapons.

Anthropic debuts on the stock market this morning, and Kenny Polcari of Slatestone explains what investors are betting on. Anthropic brought in 17 billion dollars last quarter but still posted a loss, and Polcari says investors expect it to join the group of technology names that will change how people live and work. The IPO range was raised from 70 to 78 dollars up to 80 to 85, with an 83 dollar offer price, though the opening price will reflect demand from investors who missed the allocation. Funds that got shares may sell part of their positions to lock in gains. Polcari says the Nasdaq is in correction territory, down about 11.5 percent, and some AI names like Micron are in a bear market, but he does not think the AI story is over. He expects the market to stabilize once Anthropic trades freely, as it did after the SpaceX offering.

Daily Wire reporter Jacob Wheeler explains what to expect from Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa, the first Hispanic woman to win the office after defeating Greg Abbott. Education will be a priority: she calls the nearly billion-dollar school voucher program a scam and plans to fire the Texas Education Agency head on day one, though Republicans keep the state Senate and can block changes. On immigration, Houston and Austin have changed how police work with ICE, and Hinojosa, who calls herself a border security Democrat, plans to undo Abbott's H-1B hiring freeze and the terror designation of CAIR. On costs, she plans a high cost emergency declaration freezing electricity rates, suspending the gas tax, and seeking a 1,500 dollar payment per household from the 22 billion dollar rainy day fund, which Republican senators resist.
